records.gloss: Of David. A maskil. How blessed [is the one] forgiven of transgression, covered of sin.
pieces: Of David. A maskil. How blessed is the one whose rebellion is forgiven, whose sin is covered over!

L.1: Of David. A maskil. How blessed [is the one whose] transgression [is] forgiven, [whose] sin [is] covered!

R.1: By David. A song to teach. Life is truly good for people whose wrongs God has forgiven, whose sins {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has covered over.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: maskil: probably a skillful or instructive song
decisions.reason: The word (maskil) comes from a verb meaning to be wise or to give insight; the same verb opens God's promise in verse 8 ("I will instruct you"). It heads thirteen psalms, and its exact sense as a kind of song is no longer known.

decisions.choice: forgiven, covered: sin lifted off and hidden from sight
decisions.reason: "Forgiven" (nesuy) is literally "lifted": the load of sin is carried away. "Covered" means God no longer looks on it (85:3). In verse 5 the psalmist stops covering his own sin, and God forgives it.

decisions.choice: transgression, sin: rebellion and failure
decisions.reason: Verses 1-2 use three words for wrongdoing: transgression (pesha'), a breaking away from the LORD; sin (chata'ah), missing the mark; and iniquity ('awon, verse 2), crookedness and the guilt it brings. Together they cover every kind of wrong.

decisions.choice: quoted in Romans 4:7-8
decisions.reason: Paul quotes verses 1-2 as David's words about the person whom God counts righteous apart from works (Romans 4:6-8).

decisions.choice: transgression (L); rebellion (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plain word for the meaning of pesha' (m4); the Hebrew is singular.

decisions.choice: a song to teach
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense of the term (m2).

decisions.choice: God has forgiven, he has covered over
decisions.reason: Readable names who forgives; verse 5 says it is the LORD.

records.heading: The joy of sin forgiven

records.source: אַ֥שְֽׁרֵי אָדָ֗ם לֹ֤א יַחְשֹׁ֬ב יְהוָ֣ה ל֣וֹ עָוֺ֑ן וְאֵ֖ין בְּרוּח֣וֹ רְמִיָּה׃
records.gloss: How blessed [is] a person [to whom] YHWH does not count iniquity, and [there is] no deceit in his spirit.
pieces: How blessed is anyone whose guilt {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not hold against them, who has no deceit in their spirit!

L.2: How blessed [is] a person to whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not count iniquity, and in whose spirit [there is] no deceit!

R.2: Life is truly good for people when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not hold their sins against them, and when they are not trying to hide anything.

decisions.choice: count: reckon, put to someone's account
decisions.reason: The verb (chashav) is used of crediting or charging something to a person (Genesis 15:6). The LORD does not charge the guilt to this person's account.

decisions.choice: no deceit: no hiding, no pretending
decisions.reason: The deceit is the attempt to hide sin, described in verses 3-5. The blessed person is not sinless but honest with God.

decisions.choice: a person: anyone
decisions.reason: The word ('adam) means a human being, man or woman.

decisions.choice: them, their
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "him" and "his" refer to anyone (m3); Balanced and Readable use "they", which is inclusive without a setting.

decisions.choice: are not trying to hide anything
decisions.reason: Readable says what the deceit is (m2).

records.gloss: For when I kept silent, my bones wore out in my roaring all the day.
pieces: While I kept quiet, my bones wore away with my groaning the whole day long.

L.3: For when I kept silent, my bones wore out through my roaring all the day.

R.3: When I kept my sin to myself, my body grew weak. I groaned all day long.

decisions.choice: I kept silent: I did not confess
decisions.reason: The silence is set against verse 5, where he makes his sin known. While he hid it, his suffering went on.

decisions.choice: my bones wore out: my whole body wasted away
decisions.reason: The bones stand for the whole person, body and strength (6:3; 31:11).

decisions.choice: roaring: loud groaning in distress
decisions.reason: The word (she'agah) is used of a lion's roar (Isaiah 5:29) and of cries of pain (22:2).

decisions.choice: kept my sin to myself
decisions.reason: Readable says what the silence was (m1).

records.source: כִּ֤י׀יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַיְלָה֮ תִּכְבַּ֥ד עָלַ֗י יָ֫דֶ֥ךָ נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ לְשַׁדִּ֑י בְּחַרְבֹ֖נֵי קַ֣יִץ סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: For day and night your hand was heavy on me; my sap was changed in [the] droughts of summer. Selah.
pieces: Day and night {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand pressed hard on me; the life in me dried up as in the drought of summer. Selah

L.4: For day and night {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand was heavy upon me; my sap was turned [as] by the droughts of summer. Selah

R.4: Day and night I felt {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pushing down hard on me. My strength dried up like water in the summer heat. Selah

decisions.choice: your hand was heavy: God's pressure and discipline
decisions.reason: God's heavy hand is his power felt as punishment or pressure (1 Samuel 5:6, 11). The psalmist knew his trouble came from God.

decisions.choice: sap: vigor, the moisture of life
decisions.reason: The word (leshad) is rare; in Numbers 11:8 it describes something rich with oil. Here it seems to be the freshness of life, dried up like plants in summer.

decisions.choice: was turned by the droughts: changed as in drought
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "in" the droughts of summer; the sense is a comparison, as the land dries out in the summer heat.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

decisions.choice: I felt you pushing down hard on me
alternatives: your hand was heavy on me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1).

records.source: חַטָּאתִ֨י אוֹדִ֪יעֲךָ֡ וַעֲוֺ֘נִ֤י לֹֽא־כִסִּ֗יתִי אָמַ֗רְתִּי אוֹדֶ֤ה עֲלֵ֣י פְ֭שָׁעַי לַיהוָ֑ה וְאַתָּ֨ה נָ֘שָׂ֤אתָ עֲוֺ֖ן חַטָּאתִ֣י סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: My sin I made known to you, and my iniquity I did not cover; I said, I will confess concerning my transgressions to YHWH, and you, you forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah.
pieces: I made my sin known to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; I did not hide my wrongdoing. I said, "I will own my rebellion before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} took away my sin and its guilt. Selah

L.5: My sin I made known to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and my iniquity I did not cover; I said, "I will confess my transgressions to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah

R.5: I told {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} about my sin. I stopped hiding the wrong things I had done. I said, "I will admit to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that I have rebelled." And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forgave me for all of it. Selah

decisions.choice: I did not cover: I stopped hiding it
decisions.reason: The same verb as "covered" in verse 1. When he stopped covering his sin, God covered it.

decisions.choice: you forgave: you lifted
decisions.reason: The same verb as "forgiven" in verse 1 (nasa'), "lift" or "carry away". The Hebrew stresses "you": it was God who did it.

decisions.choice: I said ... and you forgave: forgiveness followed at once
decisions.reason: The decision to confess and God's forgiveness stand side by side, with nothing between them.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

decisions.choice: own my rebellion
decisions.reason: "Own" is to admit openly that it is mine; rebellion is pesha', as in verse 1.

records.source: עַל־זֹ֡את יִתְפַּלֵּ֬ל כָּל־חָסִ֨יד׀אֵלֶיךָ֮ לְעֵ֪ת מְ֫צֹ֥א רַ֗ק לְ֭שֵׁטֶף מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֑ים אֵ֝לָ֗יו לֹ֣א יַגִּֽיעוּ׃
records.gloss: For this let every faithful one pray to you at a time of finding; surely in a flood of many waters, to him they will not reach.
pieces: So let everyone who is faithful pray to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in the time when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can be found. Even when great waters come flooding in, the flood will not reach them.

L.6: For this let every faithful [one] pray to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at a time of finding; surely in the flood of great waters, they will not reach {{gender:them|him}}.

R.6: So everyone who is loyal to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} should pray to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} while there is still time to find {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Then, when trouble rises like a flood, it will not reach them.

decisions.choice: faithful: one who is loyal to God
decisions.reason: The word (chasid) comes from chesed and means a person who keeps faith with God (4:4; 12:2).

decisions.choice: at a time of finding: while God may be found
alternatives: at a time of distress (with a small change)
decisions.reason: The words read "at a time of finding": a time when God lets himself be found (Isaiah 55:6; Deuteronomy 4:29). Some read a similar word, "distress". The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: the flood of great waters: overwhelming trouble
decisions.reason: Deep or rising waters are a common picture of danger and distress (18:17; 69:2-3).

decisions.choice: them, with "him" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Him" is the faithful person, anyone who prays (m1).

decisions.choice: when you can be found (B); while there is still time to find you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose finding is meant (m2).

decisions.choice: trouble rises like a flood
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m3).

records.source: אַתָּ֤ה׀סֵ֥תֶר לִי֮ מִצַּ֪ר תִּ֫צְּרֵ֥נִי רָנֵּ֥י פַלֵּ֑ט תְּס֖וֹבְבֵ֣נִי סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: You [are] a hiding place for me; from trouble you will guard me; [with] shouts of deliverance you will surround me. Selah.
pieces: You are my shelter where I can hide; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} keep me safe from distress and put glad cries of rescue all around me. Selah

L.7: You [are] a hiding place for me; from trouble {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will guard me; [with] shouts of deliverance {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will surround me. Selah

R.7: You are the place where I hide. You keep me safe from trouble. You surround me with happy shouts because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have rescued me. Selah

decisions.choice: hiding place: a secret shelter
decisions.reason: The word (seter) is a covert or hidden place (27:5; 91:1). He no longer hides his sin; he hides in God.

decisions.choice: shouts of deliverance: songs of joy for rescue
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual, and the first word may have arisen from the end of the word before it. As it stands it means the ringing cries of people who celebrate a rescue.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

decisions.choice: because you have rescued me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the shouts are about (m2).

records.source: אַשְׂכִּֽילְךָ֨׀וְֽאוֹרְךָ֗ בְּדֶֽרֶךְ־ז֥וּ תֵלֵ֑ךְ אִֽיעֲצָ֖ה עָלֶ֣יךָ עֵינִֽי׃
records.gloss: I will instruct you and I will teach you in [the] way which you will go; I will counsel, on you my eye.
pieces: I will give you insight and show you the road you are to take; I will advise you and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eye on you.

L.8: I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you should go; I will counsel [you, with] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eye upon you.

R.8: I will help you understand. I will teach you the way you should live. I will give you advice and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eye on you.

decisions.choice: I will instruct you: God speaks
decisions.reason: The speaker changes. It is most likely the LORD answering the one he has forgiven: "my eye on you" is his watchful care (33:18). Some take it as the psalmist teaching others what he has learned (compare 51:15).

decisions.choice: I will instruct you: I will give you insight
decisions.reason: The verb (sakal) is the root of maskil in the title (verse 1): to make someone wise and able to act wisely.

decisions.choice: my eye on you: watchful care
decisions.reason: To set the eye on someone is to watch over them for good (Jeremiah 24:6).

decisions.choice: my, as a deity pronoun
decisions.reason: Taking the LORD as the speaker (m1), "my" refers to him and follows the deity_pronoun setting.

records.source: אַל־תִּֽהְי֤וּ׀כְּס֥וּס כְּפֶרֶד֮ אֵ֤ין הָ֫בִ֥ין בְּמֶֽתֶג־וָרֶ֣סֶן עֶדְי֣וֹ לִבְל֑וֹם בַּ֝֗ל קְרֹ֣ב אֵלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Do not be like a horse, like a mule, without understanding; with bit and bridle [is] its harness to restrain [it], not coming near to you.
pieces: Do not be like a horse or mule with no sense, which needs a harness of bit and halter to rein it in, or else it will not come near you.

L.9: Do not be like a horse, like a mule, [that has] no understanding; with bit and bridle [is] its harness to hold [it] in, [else it does] not come near to you.

R.9: Do not be like a horse or a mule that does not understand. It must be controlled with a bit and reins, or it will not come to you.

decisions.choice: Do not be: spoken to all who listen
decisions.reason: The command is plural, addressed to everyone, though verse 8 spoke to one person.

decisions.choice: its harness: its gear
decisions.reason: The word ('adi) usually means ornament; here it seems to be the gear on the animal's head. Its meaning in this verse is not certain.

decisions.choice: not coming near to you: it will not come unless forced
alternatives: so that it does not come too close to you
decisions.reason: The last words are short and can be read two ways: the animal will not come to you unless it is led by force, or the gear is needed to keep it from coming at you. Either way, a person should come willingly.

records.source: רַבִּ֥ים מַכְאוֹבִ֗ים לָרָ֫שָׁ֥ע וְהַבּוֹטֵ֥חַ בַּיהוָ֑ה חֶ֝֗סֶד יְסוֹבְבֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Many pains [belong] to the wicked, but the one who trusts in YHWH, loyal love will surround him.
pieces: The wicked have many sorrows, but whoever trusts in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is surrounded by loyal love.

L.10: Many [are the] pains of the wicked, but the one who trusts in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, loyal love will surround {{gender:them|him}}.

R.10: Wicked people have many troubles. But people who trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will have {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love all around them.

decisions.choice: will surround: as in verse 7
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 7: God surrounds his people with songs of rescue and with his loyal love.

decisions.choice: loyal love: love that keeps its commitments
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that is faithful to a bond and goes beyond what is owed: the LORD's commitment to his people, shown in kindness and rescue (Exodus 34:6-7).

decisions.choice: loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12: "loyal love" keeps both the love and the faithfulness of the word; Readable says "faithful love".

decisions.choice: them, with "him" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Him" is anyone who trusts in the LORD.

decisions.choice: his faithful love
decisions.reason: Readable says whose love it is, the LORD's.

records.source: שִׂמְח֬וּ בַֽיהוָ֣ה וְ֭גִילוּ צַדִּיקִ֑ים וְ֝הַרְנִ֗ינוּ כָּל־יִשְׁרֵי־לֵֽב׃
records.gloss: Be glad in YHWH and rejoice, righteous [ones], and shout for joy, all upright of heart.
pieces: Celebrate in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and be joyful, you righteous; sing out with joy, all whose hearts are upright!

L.11: Be glad in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and rejoice, righteous [ones]; and shout for joy, all [you] upright of heart.

R.11: People who do what is right, be glad because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and celebrate! All you who have honest hearts, shout for joy!

decisions.choice: upright of heart: honest within
decisions.reason: As in 7:11; the upright in heart have nothing to hide (verse 2).

decisions.choice: in the LORD: because of him and in his presence
decisions.reason: The joy has the LORD as its reason and its center.
